Oliver — thanks, received the forecast. I've sketched three paths below and attached a spreadsheet that lays out per-month examples. High-level: we can do marginal-only or a blended retroactive true-up; we can also offer a hybrid that has a guaranteed floor + marginal top-ups to reduce bill variability.

Option A — Marginal-only ladder (default):
- Commit bands (monthly): 0-20B, 20-60B, 60-200B, 200B+
- Each band has an incremental per-token price; you pay the marginal price for tokens within that band.
- Advantage: simplest from our invoicing side, clear unit economics.

Option B — Blended effective-rate (procurement-friendly):
- We compute an effective blended rate at true-up (monthly or quarterly) and invoice that single per-token rate for the period retroactively.
- Advantage: predictable single-line rate for accounting; disadvantage: our exposure increases if usage skews above anticipated bands.

Option C — Hybrid (recommended for Skylark):
- Minimum monthly reservation (floor) at a slightly reduced blended rate.
- Marginal pricing above the floor with narrower breakpoints and a quarterly true-up that applies credits or debits to align billing.
- Carryover: unused reserved tokens can roll up to the next quarter (capped at 25% of committed tokens).

Key commercial levers you asked about:
- Breakpoint sizing and discounts: see attached StaggeredCommit_Schema_v1.xlsx for a suggested grid tailored to your forecast.
- Clawback / churn protection: we can include a 6-12 month clawback window on large credits if you terminate early.
- True-up cadence: monthly (tight), quarterly (standard), annual (rare).

I've attached a short FAQ and a worked example. If this looks directionally right, I'll pull in Aisha on approvals and get Legal/Finance templates ready.

Attachments: StaggeredCommit_Schema_v1.xlsx, Negotiation-FAQ.md

Oliver / Hannah — I pulled together a concise worked example so you can see exact invoice outcomes under the two models. See attached calc_examples.csv. Summary:

Scenario assumptions (example month):
- Baseline expected monthly tokens: 50B
- Spike month tokens: 125B (2.5x)
- Commit bands (monthly): 0-20B @$0.004/token, 20-60B @$0.0035/token, 60-200B @$0.0028/token

Marginal-only billing (what you pay that month):
- 20B @0.004 = $80,000
- 30B @0.0035 = $105,000
- 65B @0.0028 = $182,000
- Total month = $367,000 -> effective rate = $0.002936/token

Blended retroactive (quarterly true-up) — if quarter average drops back to 60B/month, we compute a blended per-token rate for quarter and invoice a single rate. For the spike month the effective rate may look lower when smoothed over the quarter, but we carry exposure until true-up. Example in attached csv shows blended effective rate for quarter = $0.0031/token

Hybrid (floor + marginal):
- You prepay floor 40B/month at blended $0.0031/token. Above-floor tokens billed marginally. During spikes, invoice volatility is reduced because 40B is at a lower blended line; marginal top-ups apply to delta.

Risks and mitigations we've modeled:
- Revenue leakage: blended retroactive that is quarterly increases vendor exposure. Mitigation: limit retroactive smoothing to quarter and cap carryover at 40% (per your ask) OR require a larger initial reservation.
- Churn clawback: 12-month clawback is acceptable with pro-rated schedule (100% of credits revert if termination <3 months, 50% between 3-9 months, 25% between 9-12 months).

I attached calc_examples.csv showing the line-by-line math you asked for. If procurement wants a single-line blended invoice, Option B + a capped carryover (40%) + the clawback schedule is implementable but we will need Legal to accept the pro-rated clawback language.
